'It was aware we were there' and 'It just disappears. Like, gone.'

The biography Fravor filed with the subcommittee for the 26 July 2023 hearing, held in the House Committee Repository under event 116282, reads in full: 'David Fravor is a retired naval pilot and Commander of VFA-41 also known as The Black Aces. He is one of the primary witness in the 2004 USS Nimitz UFO incident. He was featured in the 2008 PBS documentary Carrier and has been interviewed on Joe Rogan's podcast The Joe Rogan Experience. Fravor joined the military at the age of 17. He has a career spanning 24 years, 18 of which was as a Navy pilot. He had completed five tours to the Persian Gulf starting after Operation Desert Storm. He commanded a squadron of 12 airplanes consisting of 330 people. Fravor retired in 2006.' The grammatical slip 'one of the primary witness' is in the original. This is a document filed with a committee and held in its repository, which is what makes it Tier 1. It is a witness-supplied biography, not a Navy service record.

The testimony was sworn, and the printed record carries the mechanism. Chairman Grothman: 'Pursuant to Committee Rule 9(g), the witnesses will please stand and raise their right hands. Do you solemnly swear to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, so help you God? [Witnesses are sworn.] Mr. Grothman. Let the record show that all the witnesses answered in the affirmative.'

Under oath he gave the radar picture of the 14 November 2004 intercept, in answer to Rep. Langworthy: 'The Princeton tracked it. The Nimitz tracked it. The E2 tracked it. We never saw it on our radars. Our fire control radars never picked it up. The other airplane that took the video did get it on a radar. As soon as it tried to lock it, it jammed the radar, spit the lock and he rapidly switched over to the targeting pod, which you can do in the F-18.'

Under oath he gave the reason the aircrew were airborne at all: 'We were at a work up with all the battle groups. So, we integrate the ships with the carrier, the airwing with the carrier, and we start working. So, we were doing an air to air defense to hone not only our skills but those of the USS Princeton when they had been tracking them for 2 weeks. The problem was that there was never manned aircraft airborne when they were tracking them and this was the first day and, unfortunately, we were the ones airborne and went and saw it.'

Under oath he gave the chain by which the case reached investigators and then the public: 'It was not until 2009, until Jay Stratton had contacted me to investigate. Unbeknownst to all, he was part of the ATIP program in the Pentagon led by Lue Elizondo. There was an unofficial official report that came out that is now on the internet. Years later, I was contacted by the other pilot, Alex Dietrich, and asked if I would been contacted and I said no, but I am willing to talk. I was contacted by Mr. Elizondo, and we talked for a short period of time.' This is the provenance chain in the words of the witness, under oath.

Asked by Rep. Langworthy 'is it true that you saw, in your words, a 40-foot flying Tic Tac shaped object?', he answered under oath: 'That is correct. For some people that cannot--know what a Tic Tac is it is a giant flying propane tank.'

conflicts: Fravor's sworn statement that 'tapes were never taken' is in direct tension with the accounts attributed to USS Princeton crewmen Kevin Day and Gary Voorhis that recording media were removed by unidentified personnel who arrived by helicopter. Both can be true if the collection was aimed at Princeton's Aegis and CEC data and at Nimitz's ATFLIR tape library rather than at VFA-41 aircrew, whom Fravor confirms were never even debriefed.

label: David Fravor
narrative: Fravor is the aviator whose single intercept broke the observational record open. In November 2004 he was Commanding Officer of Strike Fighter Squadron Forty-One, the Black Aces, attached to Carrier Air Wing Eleven aboard USS Nimitz. In his sworn written statement to the House Oversight Subcommittee on National Security, the Border and Foreign Affairs on 26 July 2023 he described being vectored off a training intercept to investigate a contact the cruiser USS Princeton had been tracking, and finding 'a small white Tic Tac shaped object with the longitudinal axis pointing N/S and moving very abruptly over the white water,' with 'no Rotors, No Rotor wash, or any visible flight control surfaces.' He testified the Princeton had been watching objects descend from above 80,000 feet to 20,000 feet 'for the previous 2 weeks.' The single most load-bearing line in his statement is a negative one: 'the incident was never investigated, none of my crew were ever questioned, tapes were never taken.' That sentence is not a denial of the coverup - it is evidence of the specific shape of it. The Navy's own range fouler report on the incident, released via FOIA on 13 January 2023, records that 'Reporting terminated at 3rd Fleet, there was no process to share the reporting.' The event stayed dormant until Jay Stratton contacted Fravor in 2009 to investigate it for a DoD program, and until the New York Times published the FLIR1 video in December 2017. Fravor told 60 Minutes on 16 May 2021 the object 'was aware we were there' and that 'it just disappears. Like, gone.'
